title: Signature with a C program ("gcc_prog.")
creator: Kostas Maistrelis
origin: What the three lines of C at the bottom of the collector's Usenet signature of 1998 printed: the code exactly as in the signature, compiled with gcc -std=gnu89 and run by the collector in 2026. The signature is SIG.TXT in Asciianm.zip (10 Feb 1998) and is at the end of his two ASCIIANI posts to alt.ascii-art.animation of 12 Feb 1998
notes: An animation for the reader to compile and run, the "c-code in .sigs" of the ASCII art FAQ. It builds the collector's email address of 1998 (no longer in use) one letter at a time, from right to left: each letter slides from the start of the line to its place, with carriage returns only, no escape sequences. The pauses are 998 BEL characters after each of the 632 steps: 630,736 of the 644,337 bytes. They are kept as printed, so on a terminal with a bell it beeps, as it did in 1998. The drafts of the signature (Dec 1997 to Jan 1998) and its two versions are kept by the collector. The collector plays it at 1,800,000 baud.

title: rain ("animated raindrops display")
creator: Eric P. Scott
origin: Recorded by the collector in 2026 from rain.c of 4.2BSD (Unix History Repository, branch BSD-4_2, usr/src/games/rain.c, = tuhs.org 4.2BSD), with only the tty handling ported to Linux (sgtty to termios, marked "2026" in the ported source)
notes: A program of BSD Unix, not a file: it has no delay and draws through termcap, so its speed was the speed of the line; the later NetBSD manual says that "If the terminal is faster than 9600 baud" a delay must be set "to obtain a proper rain effect", and that it was "modeled after the VAX/VMS program of the same name". Dots, drops (o, O) and splashes (-, |.|, / \, | O |, \ /). Recorded on a 24 x 80 vt100 at 9600 baud: 115,202 bytes, 2 minutes, then stopped with Ctrl-C (SIGINT) as a user would. The NULs are the vt100 padding that rain sends itself (5 ms after each cursor move). Two fixes outside its code: a vt100 terminfo without padding on cursor-right/up, and the "$<5>" dropped from its last line, because rain prints those strings without tputs and today's padding syntax would show as text. Same bytes on every run (rand() unseeded). Its companion is worms.vt (same author, Oct 1980), recorded the same way.

title: worms
creator: Eric P. Scott
date: 1980-10 (source: "Eric P. Scott / Caltech High Energy Physics / October, 1980"); 4.2BSD 1983; this recording 2026-11-18
origin: Recorded by the collector in 2026 from worms.c of 4.2BSD (Unix History Repository, branch BSD-4_2, usr/src/games/worms.c, = tuhs.org 4.2BSD), with only the reading of the line speed ported to Linux (gtty to tcgetattr, marked "2026" in the ported source)
